title: Altair "Save as PNG" downloads a low-res blurry image
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit renders Altair plots perfectly as long as they are visualized within a browser.

However, if i want to download the graph as a .png, the downloaded file is very low quality (blurry). 

This can be validated by going here and downloading an image from any of the charts:
https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/charts/st.altair_chart

This makes it impossible to use these downloaded PNG:s in a report (powerpoint).

This seems to because altair defaults to using a PPI of 72 when rendering. Altair does support using a 'ppi' parameter when calling chart.save:
https://altair-viz.github.io/user_guide/saving_charts.html#png-figure-size-resolution

In order to create and download a higher-resolution image i can run the following code:

```python
    b = st.altair_chart(chart, use_container_width=False)

    chart.save("test.png", ppi=200)
    with open("test.png", "rb") as file:
        btn = st.download_button(label="Download image", data=file, file_name="test.png", mime="image/png")
```

**The problem with this approach is that the Streamlit theme is not used in the resulting graph.**


Is there any way to support:
* Setting PPI to be used for "Save as PNG" calls?
* Using the Streamlit theme in chart.save ?

### Reproducible Code Example
In order to create a higher-resolution image i can run the following code:
```Python
    b = st.altair_chart(chart, use_container_width=False)

    chart.save("test.png", ppi=200)
    with open("test.png", "rb") as file:
        btn = st.download_button(label="Download image", data=file, file_name="test.png", mime="image/png")

```
The problem with this approach is that the Streamlit theme is not used in the resulting graph.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/charts/st.altair_chart
2. Click "Download as PNG" from any of the charts
3. Open the blurry image from your downloads folder

### Expected Behavior

I expect a high pixel density in the downloaded image.

### Current Behavior

I get a low pixel density in the downloaded image

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.31.1
- Python version: 3.9.16
- Operating System: MacOS Sonoma 14.1.1
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_
